description: Adversary instructions in user input override system prompt.
Hidden instructions in retrieved content treated as instruction.
Legitimate tool called with harmful parameters.
Sub-agent inherits or escalates privileges without mandate transfer.
Overlapping mandates produce inconsistent state.
Adversarial content in persistent memory treated as ground truth.
Context filled with hostile content; guardrails fall out of effective attention.
Malformed or malicious arguments to structured functions.
Current behaviour diverges from declared goal.
Agent flatters user; objective accuracy degrades.
Jailbreak survives sessions via persistent memory.
Non-human-identity credential leaked; adversary impersonates agent.
Agent escapes tool-execution sandbox.
Agent gradually acts outside mandate scope.
Composite effect emerges from individually allowed tool sequence.
Agent claims 'approved/checked' without consultation.
Fabricated sensor values accepted as ground truth.
Control-plane intrusion drives actuator; cognition plane unaware.
Model + physical system co-drift over long horizon.
Model deployed at sample rate other than training rate.
Edge agent operates on cached, no-longer-valid mandate.
Sensor/accelerator degradation silently shifts inputs.
A tool, MCP server, skill or agent package is malicious or changes after approval (rug pull, tool poisoning).

name_en: Data exfiltration via tool or egress channel
description: Non-public data leaves through a permitted outbound channel (mail, HTTP call, rendered URL, commit, ticket).
One agent's faulty or manipulated output is accepted by the next agent without its own check and grows into action.
Human oversight becomes nominal: rubber-stamp approvals, agents misreporting outcomes, or agents reaching the oversight or kill-switch configuration.
An agent or agent chain does not complete a task properly: repeated steps, unrecognised termination condition, premature stop, or a final check that tests the wrong thing (MAST 1.3, 1.5, 3.1, 3.2).
